domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk's primary focus is enterprise-grade RAG architecture, covering sparse/dense retrieval, domain-specific reranking, hybrid search, and knowledge-base design for legal corpora. Harvey serves law firms across 45 countries (legal_compliance) and LanceDB provides the search and knowledge infrastructure for retrieval at scale (search_and_knowledge). The talk covers production deployment serving hundreds of law firms and a spectrum of evaluation strategies from expert review to automated metrics. Assumes familiarity with RAG, vector databases, and retrieval architectures while remaining accessible to building practitioners. Recorded conference presentation at the AI Engineer World's Fair with two speakers sharing architecture and war stories. All evidence anchors are graded as said_in_transcript with direct excerpts from the presentation.

summary: This talk addresses the challenges of building enterprise-grade RAG systems for legal domains, presented by Calvin Qi from Harvey and Chang She from LanceDB. Harvey provides AI-powered legal assistance to law firms handling drafting, analysis, and legal workflows. Data comes at three scales: on-demand uploads (1-50 documents), project vaults containing deal-specific contracts and litigation documents, and large knowledge corpuses including legislation and case laws from various countries, each potentially containing tens of millions of documents. The retrieval challenges are multifaceted. Queries from legal experts are highly complex, combining semantic understanding, implicit date filtering, specialized dataset references, keyword matching for regulation IDs, multi-part conditions, and domain jargon. An example query about covered bonds under EU directives illustrates this complexity. The data itself is domain-specific, requiring collaboration with legal experts to properly represent, index, and preprocess. Evaluation is a critical focus area. The speakers emphasize eval-driven development as key to building reliable systems, noting there is no silver bullet. They describe a spectrum of evaluation methods ranging from high-fidelity expert reviews through expert-labeled criteria evaluated synthetically, to automated quantitative metrics like retrieval precision and recall. Infrastructure requirements include reliability, smooth onboarding and scaling, data privacy with customer-segregated storage and retention policies, telemetry, and query flexibility. LanceDB addresses these needs as an AI-native multimodal lakehouse powered by the open-source lance format, which is described as 'parquet plus iceberg plus secondary indices but for AI data.' It provides fast random access for search and shuffle, fast scans for analytics and training, and uniquely supports storing large blob data alongside small scalar data. By using Apache Arrow as the main interface, lance format is compatible with existing data lakehouse tools including Spark, Ray, PyTorch, pandas, and polars. Without a unified format, AI teams waste effort keeping fragmented data copies in sync. The talk concludes with three take-home messages: domain-specific challenges require creative solutions and deep immersion with domain experts; building for iteration speed and flexibility is essential in a rapidly evolving field, grounded in solid evaluation; and new data infrastructure must recognize the multimodal, embedding-heavy, diverse-workload reality of AI at ever-growing scale.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Speaker Introductions
sections.summary: Chang She introduces himself as CEO and co-founder of LanceDB, with 20 years building data tools including co-authoring pandas. Calvin Qi leads a team at Harvey working on RAG for complex legal documents and use cases.

sections.title: Harvey Overview and Data Scales
sections.summary: Harvey is a legal AI assistant for law firms handling drafting, analysis, and legal workflows. Data comes at three scales: on-demand uploads (1-50 docs), vaults (larger project contexts like deals and data rooms), and corpuses (knowledge bases of legislation, case laws, regulations per country).

sections.title: Core RAG Challenges
sections.summary: Key challenges include scale with large dense documents, sparse vs dense retrieval tradeoffs, query complexity from expert users, domain-specific data requiring legal expert collaboration, data security and privacy for confidential deals, and system evaluation.

sections.title: Query Complexity Demonstration
sections.summary: An example query about covered bonds under EU directives illustrates the complexity of legal queries, which combine semantic aspects, implicit date filtering, specialized dataset references, keyword matches for regulation IDs, multi-part conditions across directives and articles, and domain jargon abbreviations.

sections.title: Evaluation Strategy
sections.summary: Eval-driven development is emphasized as key to building reliable systems. No silver bullet eval exists; instead a spectrum is used from high-fidelity expert reviews (expensive, highest quality) through expert-labeled criteria evaluated synthetically, to automated quantitative metrics like retrieval precision and recall (fastest iteration).

sections.title: Data Scale and Performance Requirements
sections.summary: Data sets span many countries with complex filtering and categorization. Automation via heuristics and LLM processing is applied alongside domain expert guidance. Both online (query latency) and offline (ingestion, ML experiments) performance matters. Individual corpuses can contain tens of millions of documents.

sections.title: Infrastructure Needs
sections.summary: Infrastructure must be reliable, support smooth onboarding and scaling, provide data privacy with segregated storage and retention policies, offer telemetry, and support flexible query patterns including exact matches, semantic matches, filters, and agentic navigation. Full automation is not possible.

sections.title: LanceDB Architecture
sections.summary: LanceDB is positioned as an AI-native multimodal lakehouse beyond a vector database. It stores all AI data types (images, video, audio, embeddings, text, tabular, time-series) in one table on object store. It supports both offline and online workloads with compute-storage separation, combines multiple vector columns with full-text search and reranking, offers pandas-like APIs, and supports GPU indexing at 3-4 billion vectors per table in under 2-3 hours at a fraction of traditional cost.

sections.title: Lance Format and Ecosystem Compatibility
sections.summary: The open-source lance format is the foundational innovation, described as 'parquet plus iceberg plus secondary indices but for AI data.' It provides fast random access for search and shuffle, fast scans for analytics and training, and uniquely supports storing large blob data alongside small scalar data. Traditional formats like parquet and iceberg lack random access, blob support, and efficient schema evolution. Without lance, AI teams maintain fragmented data copies across multiple systems. Lance uses Apache Arrow as its main interface, ensuring compatibility with existing lakehouse tools—Spark and Ray for distributed writes, PyTorch for training, pandas and polars for querying.

sections.title: Take-Home Messages
sections.summary: Calvin shares three take-home messages: (1) Domain-specific challenges require creative solutions—understand data structure, explicit and implicit query patterns, and immerse yourself with domain experts. (2) Build for iteration speed and flexibility given rapidly evolving tools, paradigms, and model context windows; ground this in evaluation to get good signal on system accuracy. (3) New data infrastructure must recognize the multimodal, embedding-heavy, diverse-workload reality of AI at ever-growing scale.
